```{r}
# Assuming 'data' is your data frame and 'ADM0_EN' is the column for countries
dummy_data <- model.matrix(~ ADM0_EN - 1, data = df)

# Convert the matrix to a data frame and add it back to the original data
data <- cbind(df, dummy_data)

```

```{r}
dummy_vars <- c("ADM0_ENBenin", "`ADM0_ENBurkina Faso`", "`ADM0_ENIvory Coast`", "ADM0_ENMali",  "ADM0_ENNiger",  "ADM0_ENSenegal",  "ADM0_ENTogo")
meaning_dummy_vars <- c("Benin", "Burkina Faso",
                        "`Ivory Coast", "Mali", "Niger", 
                        "Senegal", "Togo")
```

```{r}

# Variables for Saving and Credits (Section 6)


data$isBranch <- ifelse(data$Total_bran > 0, 1, 0)
data$log_bran <- log2(data$Total_bran+1)

# Define the target variable
target <- "Total_bran"


other_vars <- c("density", "frontier")
meaning_other <- c("Density (hab/km2)", "Frontier")

id_vars <- c("age", "male")
meaning_id <- c("Average adult age", "Average adult male population")

marital_status_vars <- c("married")
meaning_marital_status <- c("Married")

#religion_vars <- c("religion_1", "religion_2")
#meaning_religion <- c("Muslim", "Christian")

#education_vars <- c("educ_scol_1", "educ_scol_2", "educ_scol_3", "educ_scol_4", "educ_scol_5", "educ_scol_6", "educ_scol_7", "educ_scol_8")
#meaning_current_education <- c("Preschool", "Primary", "Sec. 1 Gen.", "Sec. 1 Tech.", "Sec. 2 Gen.", "Sec. 2 Tech.", "Post-sec.", "Higher")

highest_education_vars <- c("no_formal_education")
meaning_highest_education <- c("Formal Education: None")

#employment_7days_vars <- c("activ7j_5")
#meaning_7days <- c("Employment: Inactive (7 days)")

employment_12_months_vars <- c("employed_12m")
meaning_12m <- c("Employed (12 months)")

branch_of_activity_vars <- c("agriculture", "livestock", "trade")
meaning_branch_activity <- c("Branch: Agriculture", "Branch: Livestock/Fish", "Branch: Trade")

csp_vars <- c("self_employed")
meaning_csp <- c("Self-employed")


saving_credits_vars <- c(
  other_vars,
  id_vars,
  marital_status_vars,
  #religion_vars,
  #education_vars,
  highest_education_vars,
  #employment_7days_vars,
  #employment_12_months_vars,
  branch_of_activity_vars,
  csp_vars
)


# Meaning of the predictors 
predictor_meaning_saving_credits <- all_meanings <- c(
  meaning_other,
  meaning_id,
  meaning_marital_status,
  #meaning_religion,
  #meaning_current_education,
  meaning_highest_education,
  #meaning_7days,
  #meaning_12m,
  meaning_branch_activity,
  meaning_csp
)



# Ensure both vectors have the same length
if(length(saving_credits_vars) != length(predictor_meaning_saving_credits)) {
  stop("Length of saving_credits_vars and predictor_meaning_saving_credits must be the same")
}


# Create a data frame for Descriptive Statistics using sapply
desc_stats_saving_credits <- data.frame(
  Variable = saving_credits_vars,
  Meaning = predictor_meaning_saving_credits,
  Mean = sapply(data[, saving_credits_vars], mean, na.rm = TRUE),
  SD = sapply(data[, saving_credits_vars], sd, na.rm = TRUE),
  Min = sapply(data[, saving_credits_vars], min, na.rm = TRUE),
  Max = sapply(data[, saving_credits_vars], max, na.rm = TRUE)
)


# Display the table using gt for nice formatting
desc_stats_saving_credits %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Descriptive Statistics"
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    Variable = "Predictor",
    Meaning = "Meaning of Predictor",
    Mean = "Mean",
    SD = "Std. Deviation",
    Min = "Min",
    Max = "Max"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = vars(Mean, SD, Min, Max),
    decimals = 1
  ) %>%
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = everything()
  ) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.width = pct(100)
  )

```

```{r}
# Create the dataset with selected variables
selected_data <- data[, c(saving_credits_vars)]

# Calculate the correlation matrix (remove non-numeric columns like the target if needed)
cor_matrix <- cor(selected_data, use = "complete.obs")

# Melt the correlation matrix into a long format for ggplot
cor_matrix_melted <- melt(cor_matrix)

# Plot the correlation matrix as a heatmap
ggplot(cor_matrix_melted, aes(Var1, Var2, fill = value)) + 
  geom_tile() + 
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", high = "red", mid = "white", midpoint = 0, 
                       limit = c(-1, 1), name="Correlation") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        axis.text.y = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Correlation Matrix", x = "", y = "") +
  coord_fixed()
```

summary(est1)

```{r}
var_names <- coef_table1$Variable
var_meanings <- c("(Intercept)", predictor_meaning_saving_credits)

# Replace variable names with meanings
coef_table1$Label <- var_meanings[match(var_names, c("(Intercept)", saving_credits_vars))]

# Prepare plot data (with readable labels)
coef_plot_data <- coef_table1 %>%
  rename(
    Estimate = Estimate,
    Std_Error = `Std. Error`
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Lower = Estimate - 1.96 * Std_Error,
    Upper = Estimate + 1.96 * Std_Error
  ) %>%
  filter(Variable != "(Intercept)")  # Remove intercept if not wanted

# Plot using the human-readable labels
ggplot(coef_plot_data, aes(x = Estimate, y = reorder(Label, Estimate))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = Lower, xmax = Upper), height = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "OLS Coefficient Plot - Total Branch",
    x = "Estimate (95% CI)",
    y = "Predictors"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
formula <- as.formula(paste(target, "~", paste(saving_credits_vars, collapse = " + ")))
est1 <- lm(formula, data = data)

# Get the summary of the regression model
ols_summary1 <- summary(est1)

# Extract the coefficients matrix
coef_matrix1 <- ols_summary1$coefficients

# Convert the coefficients matrix to a data frame
coef_table1 <- as.data.frame(coef_matrix1)

# Convert row names to a column for better formatting
coef_table1 <- tibble::rownames_to_column(coef_table1, var = "Variable")



# Display using gt with color highlights for significant variables
gt(coef_table1) %>%
  tab_header(title = "OLS Regression Results - isBranch") %>%
  cols_label(
    Variable = "Predictor",
    #Meaning = "Meaning of Predictor",  # Add a column for the meaning of each predictor
    Estimate = "Estimate",
    #`Std. Error` = "Standard Error",
    `t value` = "t-value",
    `Pr(>|t|)` = "p-value"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(Estimate, `Std. Error`, `t value`),
    decimals = 2
  ) %>%
    fmt_number(
    columns = c(`Pr(>|t|)`),
    decimals = 3
  ) %>%
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = c(Variable)
  ) 

```

```{r}
# Cluster standard errors by spatial unit (e.g., municipality)
clustered_se <- vcovCL(est1, cluster = ~ ADM1_FR)

# Summary with clustered standard errors
coeftest(est1, vcov = clustered_se)
```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# Create a combined identifier for hierarchical clustering (region and country)
data$region_country <- paste(data$ADM2_FR, data$ADM1_FR, sep = "_")

# Cluster standard errors by the combined region and country variable
clustered_se <- vcovCL(est1, cluster = ~region_country)

# Display the results with clustered standard errors
coeftest(est1, vcov = clustered_se)

```
